claim: STAGE A (written before Stage B, blind): Gazette of India No. 47, New Delhi, Saturday, November 27, 1954, Part II-Section 4, S.R.O. 484 (Army Rules, 1954), printed page 300 (PDF page 10 of 103686.pdf), rule 23(3) caution sentence transcribed from image: “Do you wish to make any statement?  You are not obliged to say anything unless you wish to do so, but whatever you say will be taken down in writing and may be given in evidence.” LEGIBILITY of caution sentence (600 dpi): every word CLEAR, including 'not' before 'obliged' (crisp, unbroken). Glyph-level notes only: in 'be taken down' the 'e' of 'be' and the final 'e' of 'evidence' have a broken crossbar and resemble 'c' (printing/scan defect; word identity CLEAR in context). Punctuation as printed: colon after 'asked', opening curly double quote, question mark after 'statement' followed by double space, comma after 'so', full stop then closing curly double quote after 'evidence'. Full sub-rule (3) as printed: 'The evidence of each witness after it has been recorded as provid-ed in the rule when taken down, shall be read over to him, and shall be signed by him, or if he cannot write his name, shall be attested by his mark and witnessed as a token of the correctness of the evidence record-ed. After all the evidence against the accused has been recorded, the accused will be asked: [caution] Any statement thereupon made by the accused shall be taken down and read over to him, but he will not be cross-examined upon it. The accused may then call his witnesses, including, if he so desires, any witnesses as to character.' (line-end hyphenations 'provid-ed', 'record-ed' are typesetting; a stray dot after 'by' on line 3 is a scan speck). No erratum/corrigendum concerning r.23 in the issue (only erratum: S.R.O. No. 454 not utilised).
original_text:
After adverse evidence, the accused is invited to make a statement but is not obliged to do so; any voluntary statement is recorded and read over. The accused is not cross-examined on that statement at this stage and may call defence or character witnesses.
Use the current authenticated caution, in a language the accused understands.; Record whether a statement was made voluntarily, without suggesting silence implies guilt.; Read over the statement and document corrections.; Allow relevant defence and character witnesses in accordance with the rule.
Coercing admissions; Treating silence as proof; Using an inaccurate caution copied from an OCR error

HCE-010's paraphrase ('invited to make a statement but is not obliged to do so ... not cross-examined ... may call defence or character witnesses') is consistent with the 1954 printed text on the elements examined. COMPARISON (after Stage A and B): agrees exactly in wording with the first examination PILOT-01 PIC-10 (orchestrator, 120 dpi; same PDF, same md5 3bb93dc7..., SHA-256 prefix c5ef95a9d553685a matches); PIC-11 identity details agree. Disagrees with the India Code compilation as recorded by PILOT-01 PIC-01 ('You are obliged to say anything unless you wish to do so', no 'not'); this reviewer did not independently retrieve or view the India Code PDF (data/text/rules-army-rules-1954.txt is not present in this checkout), so that side of the conflict rests on the first examination's record. claim: On the nine archival Gazette instruments located and image-checked (1963 S.R.O. 34; 1965 S.R.O. 116 and 215; 1979 S.R.O. 188; 1988 S.R.O. 216; 1993 S.R.O. 17(E); 2003 S.R.O. 8(E); 2019 S.R.O. 17(E); 2022 S.R.O. 6(E)), none amends rule 23 of the Army Rules, 1954 (any sub-rule), so on those instruments the r.23(3) wording as notified in 1954 ('You are not obliged to say anything unless you wish to do so ...') is unchanged. This does NOT establish that r.23(3) has never been amended: at least 19 amending instruments listed in the Government's own notes, plus S.R.O. 258/2002 and anything after 6-6-2022, were not located.
